name: feat/relaydb-v1-rust-audit-suite
summary: Hardening branch for implementing RelayDB source-memory audit checks in Rust and wiring them through the Makefile.

title: Rust-First Audit Suite
summary: RelayDB source-memory audits should be implemented in Rust so the project remains self-contained around its core compiler/runtime language.
reason: Python can prototype checks quickly, but RelayDB's durable validation logic should live in Rust for trust, distribution, and consistency.

name: relay audit-memory
summary: Proposed Rust CLI subcommand for auditing RelayDB JSON/JSONL source memory before compiling it into a .relay artifact.
Top-level Rust-first workflow orchestrator for testing, compiling, verifying, auditing, graphing, packaging, and release preparation.

name: duplicates
summary: Runs Rust source-memory audit mode for duplicate anchors. Duplicate anchors should be fatal because they break stable identity.

name: missing
summary: Runs Rust source-memory audit mode for missing internal references. Missing internal anchors should fail unless explicitly marked external.

name: orphans
summary: Runs Rust source-memory audit mode for orphan nodes. Orphans are warnings by default because some standalone nodes may be intentional.

name: memory-audit
summary: Runs the full Rust source-memory graph-health audit across parseability, anchors, duplicates, missing refs, external refs, orphans, and cycles.
RelayDB audit logic should be implemented in Rust rather than Python.
reason: RelayDB is a Rust compiler/runtime project. Keeping audit logic in Rust avoids extra dependencies, improves trust, and makes the Makefile a true orchestrator instead of a language mix.
